As a disciplined, long-term investor, we invest across a wide range of asset classes, including equities, fixed income, private equity, real estate and infrastructure, with investments in over 40 countries. Headquartered in Singapore, we have 11 offices in key financial cities worldwide. Technology Group Our Technology Group (TG) builds and runs the technology behind GIC's investment and corporate activities. Within TG, Infrastructure & Cybersecurity Engineering designs, engineers and operates the networks, hosting platforms and security services that keep GIC secure, resilient and ready for the future. About The Team The Network Services & Automation team runs the shared services and engineering platforms that every other network team depends on: DNS, DHCP and IPAM, device AAA, the network management plane, monitoring and observability, and the network automation platform. What impact can you make in this role? As a Network Services & Automation Engineer, you will own GIC's core network services and the platforms behind how the network is built, changed and observed. You will make these services highly available and secure, and build the source of truth, automation and observability that let every network engineer deliver change safely and quickly. What will you do as a VP, Network Services & Automation Engineer? Own GIC's DDI services (enterprise DNS for internal, external and hybrid resolution, DHCP and IPAM), including architecture, resilience, DNS security controls and platform lifecycle on platforms such as Infoblox or equivalent. Own network device AAA: TACACS+ and RADIUS services, role-based access and command authorisation, integration with privileged access management and identity platforms, and NAC platform lifecycle where the platform is shared. Engineer the network management plane: out-of-band access, NTP, syslog, SNMP and streaming telemetry collection, configuration backup and secure management connectivity. Design and run the network observability stack (monitoring, streaming telemetry, flow analytics, synthetic testing and packet capture / brokering) across data centre, WAN, campus, cloud and AWS Outposts, providing the dashboards and alerting Network Operations uses. Build and run the network automation platform: a network source of truth (e.g., NetBox or equivalent), Ansible / Ansible Automation Platform, Git repositories and CI/CD pipelines with pre-change validation and testing. Deliver configuration compliance and drift detection against gold-standard baselines, and automate evidence for audit and regulatory reporting. Set engineering standards for network code (repository structure, peer review, testing and secrets handling) and coach engineers across the pillar to contribute safely. Evaluate and integrate tooling vendors, manage platform capacity and lifecycle, and act as the senior escalation point for DNS, DHCP, AAA and tooling incidents. Hand services and platform changes over to Network Operations against agreed acceptance criteria, and build the handover checklist (monitoring, runbooks, as-built data) into the shared pipeline for all four roles. What qualifications or skills should you possess in this role? Typically 8+ years in network engineering or network platform roles, including at least 3 years owning enterprise DDI services and/or network automation platforms. Strong enterprise networking experience across routing, switching and security in multi-vendor estates, broad enough to work credibly with every network domain and to automate it safely. Deep hands-on experience with DNS, DHCP and IPAM at enterprise scale (e.g., Infoblox, BlueCat, EfficientIP or BIND) and with TACACS+/RADIUS services (e.g., Cisco ISE). Strong automation skills in Ansible (playbooks, roles, Jinja2), Python, Git and CI/CD, including experience with a network source of truth. Experience designing monitoring and observability for multi-vendor networks (SNMP, gNMI / streaming telemetry, NetFlow / IPFIX, syslog) using commercial and open-source tooling. A product mindset: you treat internal engineers as customers and measure the adoption and reliability of the platforms you run. Nice to have CCNP / CCIE Automation (formerly DevNet), Red Hat Ansible certification or DDI vendor certifications. Experience with pre-change validation and network testing tools (e.g., Batfish, pyATS) and policy-as-code. Experience in financial services, with familiarity with MAS TRM requirements for access control and logging. What success looks like in your first 12 months? DNS, DHCP and AAA services have documented architecture, tested resilience and agreed service levels, with no single points of failure. A network source of truth and automation pipeline are in production and used by all network engineering teams, with configuration drift measured and trending down. Network Operations has observability coverage across DC, WAN, campus, cloud and AWS Outposts, with alert noise reduced and audit evidence generated automatically. A standard handover checklist runs in the pipeline and is used by all network engineering teams, with Operations sign-off recorded automatically Why join us? Work on technology that helps safeguard Singapore's reserves for future generations. Own meaningful problems at enterprise scale, with the autonomy to shape how they are solved. Join a collaborative team that values technical depth, continuous learning and doing things properly. Work at the Point of Impact We need to be forward-looking to attract the right people to help us become the Leading Global Long-term Investor. Join our ambitious, agile, and diverse teams - be empowered to push boundaries and pursue innovative ideas, share your views, and be heard. Be anchored on our PRIME Values: Prudence, Respect, Integrity, Merit and Excellence, which guides us in how we make our day-to-day decisions. We strive to inspire. To make an impact. GIC is a Great Place to Work At GIC, our offices are vibrant hubs for ideation, professional growth, and interpersonal connection. At the same time, we believe that flexibility allows us to do our best work and be our best selves. Thus, our teams come into the office four days per week to harness the benefits of in-person collaboration, but have the flexibility to choose which days they work from home and adjust this arrangement as situational needs arise. GIC is an equal opportunity employer As an employer, we passionately believe every individual brings with them unique diversity of thought and perspectives to meaningfully enrich perspectives of GIC teams to drive competitive performance. An inclusive environment yields exceptional contribution. Learn more about our Technology Group here: https://gic.careers/group/technology-group/ Our PRIME Values GIC is a values driven organization. GIC’s PRIME Values act as our compass, enabling us to fulfil our fundamental purpose and objectives. It is the foundational bedrock which governs our behaviors, our decision making, and our focus. It informs both our long-term strategy as a firm, and the way we relate to our Client, business partners and employees. PRIME stands for Prudence, Respect, Integrity, Merit and Excellence.
